LANDING PR for story #753, DECISION 0089 SLICE 3's LAST PIECE: THE CONSOLE'S RUN SCREENS READ THE PAGES, AND A KEY PRESSED WHILE A PAGE READ IS OUT MOVES THE CURSOR EXACTLY AS THE WHOLE READ WOULD. The console's run screens (the live column and the participant level) read the store's pages instead of the whole journal; a movement key pressed while a page read is out is held, in order, and applied only when that read's answer lands, against the window it answers; on a journal the pages cannot serve, the console falls back to the whole read, and that read ends the live column where the paged read does.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051, so the contribution gate can vouch for it: its review judges the whole branch from base bc36e9302.

THE BRANCH: story-753-s3-console, in this worktree at 807548fd1, on main bc36e9302 (every commit signed):
- 2d5348b79: the controller's restack of the story and rounds 753c2-753c5 (16 commits, kept as backup/753c-pre-restack), whose message lists them;
- ace8f9c9f, 881f9dc87, b19624b68 and 41a6440fc: fix round 753c6 (the held movement queue);
- 3b0ba5c59 and b61a31869: the controller's fixes for 753c6's last finding and the first landing's M1;
- 403de7ffc, 461172428 and d66fb96f2: the three held-end fixes landing 753cL2 made in its reforges;
- e31e669b9: fix round 753c7 (the end marker's ownership rule, and five functions split under the CC ceiling);
- 1ba1f96ad: coverage round 753c8 (8816091db re-signed by the controller with its tree unchanged);
- a3345bf5e, 777b2e18c and 693579e6d: landing 753cL3's three reforge fixes (a vanished view drops its held end; a backward jump holds one window and the overflow notice is drawn; a covered status line keeps the overflow notice, and the console's screens are one vocabulary);
- 807548fd1 (controller): 753cL3's C1. `tui::fits(width, height)` is the one test of whether a frame holds the console, asked by the painter, the startup refusal, the status line's notice and `HeldView` (new field `fits`), so a frame shorter than MIN_HEIGHT drops a held movement as a narrowed frame does. Regression `run_pages::tests::held_view::chief_landing_too_short_then_shown_drops_held_movement`, sharing `held_down_hidden_by` with the width case; removal control in its message.
Make no change unless the review returns a finding.

WHERE IT STANDS:
- **Landing 753cL3** (landing-pr-for-story-753-decisio-e8742bf2) parked at REVIEW-REFORGE-EXHAUSTED-MEDIUM on one finding, C1 (#753, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/753#issuecomment-6563094552). Its chief confirmed every removed guard unreachable, one settle path, one live stream, a non-blocking input loop, the scope, and console_end 40/40. The operator ruled the controller's fix and a fresh landing; 807548fd1 is that fix, and the run is concluded.
- **Landing 753cL2** (landing-pr-for-story-753-decisio-f891b877) parked at REVIEW-REFORGE-EXHAUSTED-MEDIUM after three reforges, each a held-end fix (recorded on #753, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/753#issuecomment-6545990862). Its chief found no security residual or specification defect.
- **Fix round 753c7** (fix-round-753c7-for-issue-753-de-fb06676e) closed REVIEW-RESIDUAL-OK at LOW. Its chief confirmed:
  - the held-end class is fixed by one rule: `flush_held` records the owner on the head, every resolution goes through `resolve_end`, and `resolve_end` alone consumes the owning head; a direct `G` owns its marker and consumes nothing;
  - the five splits preserve arm order and precedence: `scroll_paged` 4, `paged_at` 11, `Fetch::participant` 9, `read_views` 11, `Fetch::merge` 13.
- **Coverage round 753c8** (coverage-round-753c8-for-issue-7-a2308d63) drove the slice's first host exact-coverage misses (82 lines, 74 branches, 1 function at e31e669b9). The controller's host gate now reads exact: 79,227 lines, 9,988 branches and 10,614 functions, all covered; lints and the anchor passed. The round:
  - fixed the chief's LOW L-chief-1 with no behaviour change: `paged_at` matches the screen once, so the two `Screen::Run` arms no input could reach are gone;
  - added 56 named tests, each with a mutation that fails it by name (listed in 1ba1f96ad's message);
  - **restructured away guards it argued unreachable.** These are the round's riskiest edits, and the review's first target:
    - fetch.rs `participant_end` (the second `read_after` pass and its Kept arm; the empty-page arm), `merge` (`next_stream` now `expect`s a row, since `top_up_ready` is true only where a stream has an unread row), `extend_after` (the empty-page `break`);
    - movement.rs `Paging::Held` (passes `window_end`), `live_position` (`rows == 0`), `scroll_live` (the `Top | Bottom => unreachable!()` arm);
    - settle.rs `can_move`, `live_can`, `last_live_line` and `flush_held`;
    - brokkr-store seat_read.rs: the `stream.last <= after` skip, the `low != 0` guard, and `reach` made an `expect`.
  - Production is +170/-152; tests +1,429.

Operator rulings:
- 2026-11-02, in chat, "go with recommended" (#753, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/753#issuecomment-6564702017): 753cL3's C1, the controller's fix and a fresh landing (this run).
- 2026-10-31, in chat, "go with recommended" (#753, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/753#issuecomment-6548909921): fix round 753c7, M1 by one rule with the chief's test, the five functions split under 15 with no behaviour change; then a fresh landing (this run).
- 2026-10-30, in chat, "go with recommended" (#753, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/753#issuecomment-6533666575): 753c6's park, option 1, the controller's fix and its landing.
- 2026-10-30, in chat, "go with recommended on all the rulings" (#753, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/753#issuecomment-6519207431): fix round 753c6, option 1, held keys.
- 2026-10-29, "go with recommended on all four" (#753, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/753#issuecomment-6504746005). 2026-10-29, "Queue 753c4 (Recommended)" (#753, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/753#issuecomment-6491163641). 2026-10-28, "5a" (#753, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/753#issuecomment-6468534554): the live column's journal order. 2026-10-26, "a" (#753). 2026-10-19, "accept all for 0089" (PR #769).
- Decision 0088 (the console reads only what landed, off its input loop). Decision 0071 rulings 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11. Decision 0063 (Linux and macOS).

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks below. For a scratch, use `git worktree add` or `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into /var/tmp, never a byte copy of this worktree. It reports each finding, written as a test case: the journal set up, the keys pressed, and the frame or cursor observed against the whole read's. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

Judge, on HEAD (the base is bc36e9302):
1. **Every removed guard is truly unreachable.** For each restructure listed above, try to reach the removed arm through the real entry points: a read answering mid-settle, a page boundary moving between passes, a writer appending between two reads of one journal, a stream ending early, an empty page, a view dropped while pending, an absolute end on a one-row stream, a cursor of 0. An `expect` that a journal can make panic is a finding. A guard that looked unreachable has been reached before (#431's FIFO).
2. **The frame test is one:** `tui::fits` is the only derivation of whether a frame draws the console (painter, startup refusal, notice, `HeldView`); a held movement is dropped when its view leaves the frame by width, by height, or by any other way the frame stops drawing its pane, on both run screens. Then, **every movement moves as the whole read does:** the live column and the participant level, through the pages, with keys pressed while a read is out (single, repeated, mixed, `G`/`g`, PageUp/PageDown), across window crossings, resizes, refreshes and the whole-read fallback; a held key never moves a view it was not pressed on; a resolved end consumes exactly its owner.
3. **The whole-read fallback and the paged read count one live stream** (`live_keys`), and nothing else derives it.
4. **The input loop never blocks** (decision 0088); the held queue is bounded as stated, and a queue whose view leaves the frame is dropped whether or not its read has answered.
5. **Scope:** no change to the store or the view beyond what the branch records; heap budget values unchanged except the `detail-window` entry; files under their ceilings; no function over CC 15; no contracts/, fixtures/, policy/ or reference/ change; no new suppression.
6. For the PR, list the rulings owed, unless already ruled: the held queue's 64 coalesced movement runs (adjacent identical keys sharing a count); an overflow dropping the oldest run and cancelling its unresolved end with a status notice; the end marker's ownership rule; the API as the branch records it (brokkr-store `Store::seat_from` and its `impl` line, brokkr-view `seat_keys` and `working_participants`); the `detail-window` heap entry; and any NEW ask.

GATES (verify, and the implement phase only if a finding returns):
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-store --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-view --locked (timeout 280 each)
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked -- tui:: (timeout 280); then run_pages:: split by its submodules, each under timeout 280: `run_pages::tests::held_view`, `console_end`, `fetch_edges`, `paged_reads`, `display_clamp`, then the rest of `run_pages::`
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- seat_view:: seat_rows:: composed_view:: suppressions:: contributing:: doc_samples:: decisions_index:: doc_truth:: (timeout 280)
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --release --locked --test heap_run_view --test heap_seat_view --test heap_costs (timeout 280)
- typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; git diff --check
- If the `it` suite fails with every spawned git dying while parsing its config, your environment exports `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` without its keys (753c8 saw this; #936 is the test-side hardening). Rerun with `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_*` and `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` unset, and quote both results.
- TMPDIR stays OUTSIDE this worktree (use /var/tmp, created in the same command if missing). Before reporting, `git status --short` shows no untracked file.
- Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job pending: this seat is non-interactive.
- A seat whose commands run through the `workspace` tool has a 300-second response limit per call, and a call that outlasts it leaves its command running and blocks the calls behind it, including the write of your result file (the first landing lost its review that way, four times). Wrap every command in `timeout 280` there and split a long suite by test filter. If a gate still cannot finish inside the limit, report it UNVERIFIED (the controller's host coverage runs every test) rather than retrying it. Write your result file before any optional extra check.
- Any commit: signed off (`git commit -s`), "view: …" ending "(#753)", with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>" LAST, directly after the sign-off. Never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

KNOWN FLAKES, not this branch's: capability_broker tests and `machine_proof::` runs failing "MCP server box filesystem identity is not protected" under host load; brokkr-runtime engine::broker admission tests ending `Identity(Expired)` under load; brokkr-protocol `oneshot::tests::a_produced_attempt_carries_its_result_and_checkpoints` (#932); heap_costs' one-byte compare difference under load. If verify fails on one of these alone, the implement visit reruns it on the host alone (`-- --exact`, with HOME set), quotes both results, makes no commit, and reports COMPLETE, not blocked.

CONTENTION (NEVER message the-forge-9d or any brokkr-wt-* seat): #907 is in the dsh console; #430 slice 4a (another lane) holds brokkr-protocol adapters.rs; decision 0065 slice two's U9b1e (another session) is in brokkr-cli broker.rs, broker/session.rs, broker/rpc.rs and the capability_broker enabled suite; 9d's CI work owns ci.yml and the coverage and test-shard scripts. Leave them.

YOUR SEAT: you run on dsh (DeepSeek Flash, DeepSeek's platform), unboxed with dsh's own tools, at the operator's word (2026-10-26). Sign off every commit (`git commit -s`).

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json

  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/verify"},

Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest.     {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],

    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
```
